latin_text: haec illa pax quam facit Deus in excelsis suis, quam angeli in terram descendentes annuntiarunt hominibus bonae voluntatis, ut per eam ipsi homines ascendentes in caelum angeli fierent.
english_translation: that peace which God makes in His heavens, which the angels who came down to earth announced to men of good will so that these men would, ascending to heaven, be transformed by it into angels.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico invokes the Lucean nativity narrative (Luke 2:13-14: the angelic announcement of Christ's birth) to establish angels as soteriological mediators. The angels descend to announce *pacem quam facit Deus* (*the peace that God makes*) to humans *bonae voluntatis* (of good will—those capable of receiving divine grace). This peace is not merely psychological tranquility but soteriological reconciliation: the restoration of cosmic and personal harmony through Christ's incarnation. The reciprocal movement is essential: *ut per eam ipsi homines ascendentes in caelum angeli fierent* (so that through it these very humans, ascending to heaven, would become angels).

The philosophical function is to establish the reciprocal mediation between angelic and human orders. Angels do not descend to remain in transcendence; they descend to elevate humanity. Humans do not merely receive knowledge; they receive the invitation and power to ascend. The announcement of peace (*pax*) is not a static declaration but an opening of the way—a removal of the barrier between terrestrial and celestial realms. [VERIFIED] The Christian Incarnation (God becoming human in Christ) establishes the theological foundation for human becoming angelic: if God descended to assume human nature, humans can ascend to participate in divine nature through Christ. The angels are the primary exemplars and mediators of this exchange.

[INFERRED] This passage connects to the entire Passion narrative as Pico understands it: Christ's kenosis (self-emptying descent) enables human exaltation (ascent). Heptaplus 7.4 (the seventh day/Christological fulfillment) parallels this soteriological structure. The Commento Book III-IV integrates the incarnational mystery into the mystical theology of angelic transformation. Being & Unity grounds this theologically: Christ's assumption of human nature is the perfect instance of creature receiving divine being, establishing the metaphysical possibility of all creaturely participation in divinity.
notes: Angelology and soteriology converge: angels descend to announce peace, enabling humans to ascend and become angels. The angels function as mediators between the transcendent and immanent realms.
